To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the majority of links in the Web point from the United States to other English-language sites; 2) the Web is not a single, unified community; 3) the majority of Web pages have few links to other sites; and 4) the majority of the Web is not linked to the majority of the rest of the Web.
• The Web has a strong, positive correlation with the real-world social network of the United States.
1) the Web is a very complex system, and 2) the Web is very different from the systems studied in the social science literature.

the social factors that influence link creation on the World Wide Web.
the question: what do the links on the Web mean?
the social science aspects of the Web, in particular the social factors underlying link formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no Theory of Link Analysis.
the Web does not have a theory, and that link analysis research cannot be done in the way we are used to doing it.
the Web is not capable of giving definitive answers on social science questions concerning the creation of links.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Web is an excellent source of data for social science research.
the Web is not an ideal environment in which to conduct social science link analysis, but that it is possible to use link analysis to investigate the Web.
link analysis is a powerful tool for understanding social phenomena on the Web, but it is a blunt instrument.
The main takeaway from our work is that
link analysis is an inherently social process.
link analysis research is best conducted by using a range of methodologies, and then interpreting the results using a combination of qualitative and quantitative approaches.
link analysis is a very complex and difficult area.
